changes: Added 'owner' to Giridhara's roles: 'svārthaṃ' means he copied it for his own use, which makes him owner as well as scribe ('parārthaṃ ca' adds that it is also for others).
Added the second spelling of the author's name in the closing verse (kālidaś, corrupt for Kālidāsa) to the notes; Kālidāsa stays as author only.
Expanded the notes: the catalogue's scribe name (Girirājabhaṭṭa) and date (VS 1732) conflict with the colophon; possible reading of the place name; how ce_approx was worked out.

persons.name: Giridhara
persons.evidence: likhitam idaṃ kāvyaṃ bhaṭṭagiridhareṇa svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca

purpose: svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca (for himself and for others)
notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as Girirājabhaṭṭa and the date as VS 1732. The colophon clearly reads 'bhaṭṭagiridhareṇa' and 'saṃvat 1737', so either the catalogue is wrong or the cataloguer misread the manuscript. The era is not named, but 'saṃvat' in a Devanagari manuscript points to VS. VS 1737 = CE 1680 (Āśvina, so September–October 1680 if the year starts in Caitra). It would be 1681 if the year starts in Kārttika. 'sarojapuṭabhedane' = 'in the town (puṭabhedana) of Saroja'. Saroja means 'lotus', so this may be a Sanskrit rendering of a place name like Kamala-/Padma-pura. It cannot be identified, so normalized is left empty. The verse after the colophon ('itthaṃ bhūtaṃ sucaritam ...') is an addition with errors ('vinodi (!)', 'nitinipuṇatāṃ' for nīti-, 'kālidaś' for Kālidāsa). It names only the author, not any other person.
